description: p4-temportal's hooks. run-hook.sh runs p4_memory.py and scratchpad.py at SessionStart, where scratchpad notebook-out hands Claude Code the notebook's folder as watchPaths, and at FileChanged it runs scratchpad notebook-changed, which moves a log, a build output or a binary added to the notebook into its .out/ at once. The FileChanged entry has no matcher, so it adds no file to the watch list, runs for every watched file, and moves nothing for a path outside the notebook. Each entry sets onFailure to continue, so a runner that cannot start, as on Windows without Git Bash, blocks nothing. register.ts is the hooks module, whose functions run inside Claude Code: it finds the python the runner proved, asking p4-native's capability map first whether this is Windows where no runner proved one, and runs the retention sweep, lifetime.py tick, at a session's start, on its timer while the session runs, and in a process let go of at the session's end, where SessionEnd command hooks share 1.5 seconds that a plugin's timeout does not raise. It registers the slash command /lifetime, whose list, set, clear and now each run lifetime.py's command of that name, and the same four as the tool lifetime for the model, served at tool.run once Claude Code allowed the call, and at tool.call on Claude Code 2.1.330, where no glob selects tool.run and the allowed call comes back up with the engine's answer that no hook served it. At session.compact, the event of every compaction, it adds a keep list to what the summary is told and builds the list of the files the session wrote or edited, which it hands as additional context of the SessionStart that Claude Code raises inside a compaction, so the list is an attachment of that hook and no message. A minute after a turn of the main conversation ended it compacts the session itself, by $.session.compact and by running /compact with no words after it where Claude Code refuses that call, once the context is at or past temportal.compact_at, which is 70 percent unless p4.json sets it and 0 for none. At classic.SessionStart, above every SessionStart command hook, it reads each source of the settings by $.settings.read and adds the keys p4 reads to the hook input as p4_settings, so p4conf.py's settings keeper takes the managed settings from Claude Code and p4_memory.py all four sources, and both read the settings files where the input holds none. At classic.PostToolUse it notes each plan file a session creates or writes again in a folder named plans, and the last sweep copies the ones in Claude Code's own plans folder into the store's temportal/plan-planner where plansDirectory names that folder, since the key holds from the session after the one whose start wrote it, and leaves the original, which a session resumed later still writes. The PreCompact entry runs compact.py keep, which prints the same keep list as the summary's instructions for a session where the module does not load, and prints nothing where the instructions it is handed already hold the list, as they do beneath the module. The SessionStart entry for the source compact stays, since the event hands a hook no summary to read and a hooks module does not load in every session.
